page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v5 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores through simultaneous multithreading. System memory measures 192 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard general purpose ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. The instance integrates 1933 GB of local SSD temporary storage and does not include hardware GPU acceleration. Instruction capabilities include AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration, while AVX-512 extensions are not supported.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-core processing throughput, placing the instance in the top quartile for tests such as stress-ng multi-core (64761.13), PassMark CPU (51568.07), and Geekbench multi-core (15999.0). Cryptographic benchmark performance and multi-threaded decompression (238.09 GB/sec in bzip3) are similarly strong. Memory operations demonstrate sustained uncached read bandwidth of 106.09 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 58.51 GB/sec. While CPU-based text generation for small 135M parameter language models achieves 320.66 tokens/sec, large 70B parameter models yield 2.54 tokens/sec, highlighting CPU execution boundaries on heavy neural workloads.

With its combination of high core counts, predictable memory ratios, and bundled high-capacity local SSD storage, the instance delivers high resource density for multi-tenant and parallel architectures. The hardware profile fits enterprise relational and NoSQL databases, batch transformation pipelines, continuous integration build clusters, and microservice backends, whereas workloads requiring AVX-512 instructions or heavy machine learning generation require alternate hardware profiles.

Synthetic benchmarks show top-quartile parallel processing capability, with strong scores in PassMark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded decompression tests. Memory bandwidth measures 106.09 GB/sec for uncached reads and 58.51 GB/sec for uncached writes. While small-scale CPU language model inference is feasible, large model generation shows substantial latency. The hardware balance and high-speed local disk accommodate enterprise databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, and high-concurrency web application tiers.
